daemon_body.description: A daemon's JSON answer, passed through unchanged (C-10.17), whole: in result.daemon on success, in error.daemon (with error.daemon_status) on a refusal. Its shape is web-chat's; the route that produced it is named by the request type. When the connector refused (05 C-05.30) it is the connector's body as received: 04's refusal body with authority, or {ok: false, connector: true, reason: 'not-running'} (C-10.17). For StartChat and StopChat (amendment A-10.3, C-10.14b) a refused answer carries here the connector's chat.status body (06-chat-status.json) whose state is refused or failed, with no daemon_status, since nothing crossed HTTP.

cookie.description: A user session (03 C-03.5, C-03.6): the cookie __Host-swc_s on the hub apex, as the shell and the phone send it. With it the request passes the CSRF rule of 04 C-04.23. Exactly one of this or the x-api-key pair is present.

x-api-key.description: An API key's id (03 C-03.7, schemas/03-credential.json api_key): a user's key, or svc_home's key for Home's MCP server (C-03.16). Sent with x-api-secret.

x-api-secret.description: The API key's secret (03 C-03.7): sws_ and 43 base64url characters.

x-swc-api.description: The API major version the client speaks (C-10.29).

x-request-id.description: Optional client id for the request, echoed as request_id; the hub mints one when absent.

idempotency-key.description: On /write and /execute: the same key within 24 hours does not act again: a hub-answered type answers the first result, a relayed type answers `conflict` (C-10.11, C-10.17 as A-10.2 amends them).

headers.description: Request headers, lowercase as Node reads them. Authentication is one of contract 03's two hub-API credentials (C-03.5 to C-03.7, C-03.16): the user session cookie, or an API key as X-Api-Key plus X-Api-Secret. There is no bearer form; one would be an addition to 03-credential.json first.

type.description: The request type; its group is the path (C-10.12).

params.description: The type's params; {} when it takes none.

type.description: The request's type, echoed when the body named one.

code.description: The error word. Clients treat an unknown word as a generic failure (C-10.29).

hint.description: What to do next, written for the person reading it, as web-chat's refusal hints are.

field.description: bad_request: the first bad field, as a JSON pointer into params.

need.description: forbidden: what the type needs (a level on a chat, a role, or a principal kind).

daemon_status.description: A relayed answer: the HTTP status as the hub received it, the daemon's or the connector's own refusal (05 C-05.30), beside the body in daemon (C-10.17).

error.description: The error shape every type shares. HTTP status per code is in C-10.13. A relayed answer maps by status first (C-10.17): a 2xx with ok:false is refused, 404 not_found, 403 forbidden with need (logged as a second lock), 400 or 415 internal, 503 unavailable, 500 relay_failed; each carries daemon and daemon_status. A relayed answer can be the connector's (05 C-05.30): a 403 whose body carries 04's authority object is forbidden, logged as a connector refusal, never a second lock; a 404 whose body is {ok: false, connector: true, reason: 'not-running'} is the connector's not_found, never the daemon's. A 502 is relay_failed and a 504 relay_timeout. Any other status is relay_failed. daemon_status is the status as the hub received it.

tailnet_name.description: The machine's Tailscale MagicDNS name as its connector last reported it (05 machine.facts tailnet_name, A-05.2), without the trailing dot. With login, the ssh target (`<login>@<tailnet_name>`) and the ssh-remote authority of every command below. Null when the machine reported none (no Tailscale, or a connector before A-05.2); then every command is null with unavailable no-tailnet.

login.description: The Unix user the connector runs as (05 machine.facts login, A-05.2). The hub writes it into every command as `<login>@<tailnet_name>` (the launcher runs as the connector's OS user and a tmux server is per user, so an ssh as any other user finds no wc-<label>; a bare ssh would send the client's local user name, which differs across the user's machines; Q-A10.1-4) and shows it beside them. Null when not reported; then the commands carry the bare host.

online.description: True while the machine's liveness state is online (07 C-07.34). The session and the commands come from the last status and assignment the hub holds; when this is false they may be stale.

machine.description: The machine the chat lives on. Its tailnet_name and login are machine facts shown here only (05 C-05.18 as A-05.2 amends it), never in the machine row of ListMachines or GetMachine.

display.description: The folder's display path, the home directory shown as ~ (06 C-06.13, 11 C-11.6), for the eye beside the commands. The real path appears only inside commands.shell and commands.code.

folder.description: The offered folder of a folder chat. Null for a repo or space chat: its root is an owned root whose path the connector never reports (06 C-06.14), so the hub holds no path for it.

name.description: 06-chat-status.json session.attach.name (A-06.1): the tmux session name the launcher created, wc-<chat-label> and nothing else (06 C-06.26), the same pattern as 06's. The hub copies it and never composes it; the commands use it as the exact-match target '=<name>'.

session.description: The connector's multiplexer session as the chat's last status reported it (06-chat-status.json session.attach, A-06.1): non-null only for a connector-launched session whose tmux session answered. Null in manual mode, when no session runs, or when the status predates A-06.1.

launch.description: How the chat's agent session starts, from its current assignment (06-chat-assignment.json agent): none when agent.want is none, else agent.launch.

terminal.description: Attach to the chat's live Claude Code session: `ssh -t <login>@<tailnet_name> tmux attach-session -t '=<session.name>'` when session is non-null (the exact-match target, quoted by C-10.14a's rule since `=` is outside the safe set); `ssh -t <login>@<tailnet_name> claude-web-chat connect attach <chat-label>` when session is null and launch is manual (06 C-06.26's manual mode, which passes the trust dialog), and when session is null, launch is connector and the chat's last status reason is needs-trust, no-tmux or home-launch-off (a Start cannot succeed there, 06 C-06.26; the manual form is always available). Null when session is null, launch is connector and no such reason stands (unavailable start-first: Start the session with StartChat, amendment A-10.3, then read again), when launch is none (no-agent), or when tailnet_name is null (no-tailnet, which decides first). A null login leaves the bare host. Never `tmux new -A`.

shell.description: A login shell in the chat's root over ssh. Folder chat: `ssh -t <login>@<tailnet_name> 'cd <path> && exec "$SHELL" -l'`, the real path quoted as C-10.14a says (`&&` and `exec "$SHELL" -l` are the template's fixed text, not words the rule builds). Repo or space chat (folder null): `ssh -t <login>@<tailnet_name> claude-web-chat connect shell <chat-label>`, since the machine's own CLI resolves an owned root (06 C-06.26a). A null login leaves the bare host. Null only when tailnet_name is null.

code.description: Open the chat's root in VS Code over Remote SSH: `vscode://vscode-remote/ssh-remote+<login>@<tailnet_name><path>` (VS Code takes `ssh-remote+user@host`), the absolute real path, percent-encoded only where RFC 3986 requires. A null login leaves the bare host. Null for a repo or space chat (unavailable owned-root: the hub holds no path) and when tailnet_name is null.

unavailable.description: One key per null command, naming why (C-10.14a): no-tailnet (the machine reported no tailnet_name), start-first (a connector-mode chat with no live session whose last status names no reason a Start cannot clear: Start it (StartChat, amendment A-10.3, C-10.14b), then read again; with needs-trust, no-tmux or home-launch-off, terminal is the manual attach instead and no key is written), no-agent (the chat wants no agent session), owned-root (a repo or space chat, whose path the hub never holds). Empty when every command is set. A client reads the reason here rather than deriving it: it depends on four fields and on the status reason the result does not carry (Q-A10.1-1).

commands.description: Commands for the user's terminal and editor, composed and quoted by the hub from the fields above (C-10.14a): tailnet_name null decides first, then the first row of C-10.14a's table that matches. Text to copy, never a credential: the ssh login is Tailscale SSH or the user's own keys. The CLI builds its own argument lists from the fields and passes on only `code`, as one argument to the OS URL opener (06 C-06.26a).

result_GetChatAttach.description: Result of GetChatAttach (amendment A-10.1, C-10.14a): the terminal attach details of one chat. Served only at daemon_level full on the chat or to the machine's pairing user; every served read is an attach.read Activity entry.

chat_id.description: The chat. Minted by the hub; its form is contract 03's.

params_StartChat.description: Params of StartChat (amendment A-10.3, C-10.14b). Group: /execute. Answered by: hub, then a connector command (05 C-05.26: chat.assign with desired running, answered by the connector's chat.status); nothing is relayed to the daemon. Needs: daemon_level full on the chat (04 C-04.4: Read and any of Message, Write page or Files), from the owner's always or a grant record the user made (C-04.2, C-04.3), never a default (as GetChatAttach, C-10.14a; R24): the owner always, another principal by a grant the user made (none for Home in v1, C-10.14b); a principal without Read answers not_found (C-10.13), one holding Read but not full answers forbidden with need. Each issued revision is a chat.start Activity entry (03's kind). Records the chat's desired state as its next assignment revision and sends it; idempotent on a chat already so (C-10.14b).

chat_id.description: The chat. Minted by the hub; its form is contract 03's.

machine_id.description: The machine the chat lives on, where the assignment went. Never null: a chat with no machine answers conflict (C-10.14b).

desired.description: The chat's desired state as the hub now records it (06-chat-assignment.json desired, 05 C-05.26): running.

rev.description: The assignment revision that carries it (06 C-06.15): a new rev when this request changed the desired state, or re-issued it after a refused or failed status for the rev in force; else the rev already in force.

changed.description: True when this request issued a new rev and wrote its chat.start Activity entry; false when the desired state was already running and the last status for that rev did not say refused or failed: nothing sent, no entry written, no wait (C-10.14b).

applied.description: True when, within the hub's wait (C-10.14b, at most 10 s), the connector's chat.status for this rev (status.rev at or above rev) reported state running. False when the machine is offline (stale true), when the status is still preparing or starting at the end of the wait, or when the hub holds no status for this rev yet; the client then follows the chat's status (07 C-07.5 chat.daemon events, GetChat). A refused or failed status answers the error refused instead.

stale.description: True when the chat's machine is offline (07 C-07.34): status is the last one it reported (05 C-05.27) and the assignment waits, sent on the machine's next hello.ack.

status.description: The chat's status as 06 reports it, whole (06-chat-status.json: its chat_id is the chat label, 03 section 2; states, counts, times and ids only, 11 C-11.1 row (d)), the newest the hub holds after the wait; null when the connector has never reported this chat.

result_StartChat.description: Result of StartChat (amendment A-10.3, C-10.14b): the recorded desired state, its revision and the chat's status as the connector reports it.

chat_id.description: The chat. Minted by the hub; its form is contract 03's.

stop_mode.description: 06 C-06.22's mode, optional. release (the default): the hold closes and the daemon's idle grace ends it once nothing retains it; a live channel bridge retains, so a chat whose agent session is up reports stopping until that session ends. now: POST /api/shutdown with X-WC-Shutdown, only on a daemon with started_by connector or on an owned root; a daemon the user started on an offered folder (other) is only released. The shell's confirmed Stop sends now (R33, DM-21). A now after a release is a change (C-10.14b).

params_StopChat.description: Params of StopChat (amendment A-10.3, C-10.14b). Group: /execute. Answered by: hub, then a connector command (05 C-05.26: chat.assign with desired stopped, answered by the connector's chat.status); nothing is relayed to the daemon. Needs: daemon_level full on the chat (04 C-04.4: Read and any of Message, Write page or Files), from the owner's always or a grant record the user made (C-04.2, C-04.3), never a default (as GetChatAttach, C-10.14a; R24): the owner always, another principal by a grant the user made (none for Home in v1, C-10.14b); a principal without Read answers not_found (C-10.13), one holding Read but not full answers forbidden with need. Each issued revision is a chat.stop Activity entry (03's kind). Records the chat's desired state as its next assignment revision and sends it; idempotent on a chat already so with the same stop_mode (C-10.14b).

chat_id.description: The chat. Minted by the hub; its form is contract 03's.

machine_id.description: The machine the chat lives on, where the assignment went. Never null: a chat with no machine answers conflict (C-10.14b).

desired.description: The chat's desired state as the hub now records it (06-chat-assignment.json desired, 05 C-05.26): stopped, with the stop_mode the request named (release by default; 06 C-06.22).

rev.description: The assignment revision that carries it (06 C-06.15): a new rev when this request changed the desired state, or re-issued it after a refused or failed status for the rev in force; else the rev already in force.

changed.description: True when this request issued a new rev and wrote its chat.stop Activity entry; false when the desired state was already stopped and the last status for that rev did not say refused or failed: nothing sent, no entry written, no wait (C-10.14b).

applied.description: True when, within the hub's wait (C-10.14b, at most 10 s), the connector's chat.status for this rev (status.rev at or above rev) reported state stopped. False when the machine is offline (stale true), when the status is still stopping at the end of the wait, or when the hub holds no status for this rev yet; the client then follows the chat's status (07 C-07.5 chat.daemon events, GetChat). A refused or failed status answers the error refused instead.

stale.description: True when the chat's machine is offline (07 C-07.34): status is the last one it reported (05 C-05.27) and the assignment waits, sent on the machine's next hello.ack.

status.description: The chat's status as 06 reports it, whole (06-chat-status.json: its chat_id is the chat label, 03 section 2; states, counts, times and ids only, 11 C-11.1 row (d)), the newest the hub holds after the wait; null when the connector has never reported this chat.

result_StopChat.description: Result of StopChat (amendment A-10.3, C-10.14b): the recorded desired state, its revision and the chat's status as the connector reports it.
